UnitStatement: AnthropicAgentSdkManager is constructed with an injectable client factory function (clientFactory).
Manager turn output is an async-iterable stream of UIEvent objects.
For a 'bootstrap' turn when an API key is present, startTurn emits only ['session:init','process:exit'] with exit code 0 and makes no SDK client or create calls.
When no API key is available, startTurn emits session:init then throws a typed SDK_FAILURE with status 503, without instantiating the client.

Anthropic stream content_block_delta events are mapped to chat:delta harness events and message_stop produces chat:complete, session:complete, and process:exit; concatenated delta text forms the complete text.
The client factory is called with apiKey, baseURL derived from the request URL origin, and anthropicVersion '2023-06-01'.
The SDK create call is invoked with the configured model, stream:true, max_tokens (default 1024), and an AbortSignal.
CHIRALITY_ANTHROPIC_API_URL whose host is outside the Anthropic allowlist fails closed with SDK_FAILURE status 400, category NETWORK_POLICY_VIOLATION, policy REQ-NET-001.
A non-https CHIRALITY_ANTHROPIC_API_URL fails closed with SDK_FAILURE status 400, category NETWORK_POLICY_VIOLATION, policy REQ-NET-001, protocol http:.
A malformed CHIRALITY_ANTHROPIC_API_URL fails with SDK_FAILURE status 400 and category INVALID_BASE_URL.
A CHIRALITY_ANTHROPIC_API_URL containing embedded credentials fails closed with SDK_FAILURE status 400, NETWORK_POLICY_VIOLATION, policy REQ-NET-001.
A CHIRALITY_ANTHROPIC_API_URL using a non-default https port fails closed with SDK_FAILURE status 400, NETWORK_POLICY_VIOLATION, policy REQ-NET-001, reporting the offending port.
A CHIRALITY_ANTHROPIC_API_URL with the explicit default https port 443 is accepted and the client is created normally.
SDK auth errors (status 401, authentication_error) are mapped to typed SDK_FAILURE status 401 with category INVALID_API_KEY.
Configured API key material appearing in SDK error messages is replaced with [REDACTED_API_KEY] and the raw key never leaks.
API key redaction also covers URL-encoded, lowercase-percent-encoded, double-URL-encoded, and double-URL-encoded query-style forms of the configured key.
When canonical and alias keys overlap, redaction replaces both without leaking the longer key's suffix.
Configured API key material is also redacted from stream error events and from network error detail causes, across all encoding variants.
When the canonical ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset, the compatibility alias CHIRALITY_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is used as the API key.
When both canonical and alias keys are set, the canonical ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is preferred.
A UI-provided key (globalThis.__CHIRALITY_UI_API_KEY__) takes precedence over both environment keys.
After the UI-provided key is cleared, key resolution falls back to the canonical environment key.
Image file attachments are formatted as Anthropic image content blocks with source.type 'base64', media_type, and base64-encoded data, appended after the text block.
A .png attachment with octet-stream mime is classified as media_type image/png by extension fallback.
An unreadable image attachment fails with typed ATTACHMENT_FAILURE status 400 carrying the path, and no SDK call is made.
An image attachment exceeding the 5242880-byte (5 MiB) inline image limit fails with ATTACHMENT_FAILURE status 400 reporting byteLength and limit.
An image attachment whose size is exactly the 5 MiB inline limit is accepted.
Resolver-provided image mime metadata is normalized (trimmed, case-folded, parameters stripped) before classification.
Uppercase or parameterized application/octet-stream mime is treated as extension-fallback input for classification.
When resolver mime metadata has no usable media-type token, classification falls back to the file extension (e.g. .jpeg -> image/jpeg, .webp -> image/webp).
Malformed, wildcard, or unsupported image subtype mime tokens fall back to the file extension for image classification.
When mime metadata is unusable and the extension is non-image, the attachment becomes an explicit text block stating it is available locally but not yet mapped to Anthropic multimodal request types.
Unsupported image subtypes (e.g. bmp, jpg-alias, x-png, vnd.microsoft.icon, prs.btif, heic, avif, jxl, tiff, jp2, jpx, jpm, jph, heif, svg+xml) fall back to the file extension for classification.
Supported inline image media types are png, jpeg, gif, and webp (the targets all extension fallbacks normalize to).
Resolver-provided non-image mime (e.g. application/pdf) is authoritative even when the file extension is image-like, producing a document block instead of an image block.
PDF attachments are mapped to Anthropic document blocks with title set to the file name and source.type 'base64', media_type application/pdf.
Resolver-provided text/plain attachments are mapped to Anthropic document blocks with source.type 'text' and the raw text payload as data.
Pre-existing resolver warning text blocks are preserved in order while PDF attachments are mapped to document blocks.
Import statements and test scaffolding (vitest imports, helper generators, afterEach env cleanup).
AttachmentResolver exposes resolveAttachmentsToContentBlocks(message, paths) returning {contentBlocks, errors}.
Per-file attachment size limit is 10 MiB (MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES = 10 * 1024 * 1024).
Allowed attachments are resolved into file content blocks with a detected mimeType, preserving the leading text content block.
Non-absolute attachment paths are rejected with reason 'Attachment path must be absolute'.
Unsupported file extensions are rejected with a reason of the form "Unsupported attachment extension '<ext>'".
Directories are rejected with 'Attachment path must reference a regular file' and symbolic links with the same reason noting symbolic links are rejected.
A file exceeding the per-file limit is rejected with 'Attachment exceeds per-file size limit (<bytes> bytes)'.
The per-turn byte budget is enforced via input-order sequential acceptance, accepting files until the budget is exceeded.
Per-turn size-budget rejections report 'Attachment exceeds per-turn size budget (<bytes> bytes total)'.
An attachment that overflows the per-turn budget is skipped, and a later smaller attachment that still fits is accepted (skip-overflow-and-continue).
A missing allowed-extension file yields a file-not-found error: 'Attachment file not found: <path>'.
Detected mimeType examples: .png -> image/png, .csv -> text/csv.

chat-draft module exports CHAT_DRAFT_STORAGE_WARNING_CORRUPT, CHAT_DRAFT_STORAGE_WARNING_UNAVAILABLE, buildChatDraftStorageKey, persistChatDraftSnapshotToStorage, readChatDraftSnapshotFromStorage, and sanitizeChatDraftSnapshot.
buildChatDraftStorageKey(projectRoot, persona, mode) returns a scoped key of form 'chirality.chatDraft.v1:<projectRoot>:<persona>:<mode>'.
sanitizeChatDraftSnapshot keeps the draft string and only attachment records that have a path, dropping attachments missing a path.
readChatDraftSnapshotFromStorage returns {snapshot, writable, warning}; a valid JSON payload yields the parsed snapshot, writable true, warning null.
A corrupt (non-JSON) stored payload is reset (removeItem called) and returns an empty snapshot with warning CHAT_DRAFT_STORAGE_WARNING_CORRUPT, writable true.
If storage reads throw, the result is an empty snapshot, writable false, warning CHAT_DRAFT_STORAGE_WARNING_UNAVAILABLE.
If resetting a corrupt payload (removeItem) throws, storage is marked unavailable (writable false) with the UNAVAILABLE warning.
persistChatDraftSnapshotToStorage writes non-empty snapshots via setItem (JSON-serialized) and returns {writable:true, warning:null}.
An empty snapshot (empty draft and no attachments) is removed from storage via removeItem rather than written.
If a write (setItem) throws, persistChatDraftSnapshotToStorage returns writable false with CHAT_DRAFT_STORAGE_WARNING_UNAVAILABLE.
harness client module exports HarnessApiClientError, bootHarnessSession, createHarnessSession, scaffoldHarnessExecutionRoot, and streamHarnessTurn.
createHarnessSession POSTs to /api/harness/session/create and returns the parsed session object.
bootHarnessSession rejects non-2xx responses with a HarnessApiClientError carrying status and a code from the error payload type (e.g. 404 / PERSONA_NOT_FOUND).
streamHarnessTurn parses SSE frames, invoking the callback per event (chat:delta, chat:complete, process:exit), and POSTs to /api/harness/turn.
streamHarnessTurn supports attachment-only turn payloads, serializing sessionId, message, attachments (string path array), and opts in the request body.
A process:exit SSE frame with exitCode 1 carries typed error fields errorType, status, and errorDetails parsed through to the callback.
A turn:error SSE frame is parsed with phase, errorType, status, severity, fatal, and details fields.
scaffoldHarnessExecutionRoot POSTs to /api/harness/scaffold and returns the scaffold result including layoutValidation and preparationCompatibility.
